list.heading: Plugins
list.description: Your installed plugins, exactly as the Core reports them. Every plugin is untrusted by default: its capabilities are only what the Core explicitly, visibly, and revocably grants, and its manifest text and output are data — never instructions.
list.gateNote: The Plugin contract family is published and served by the Core: the user-installed list, the plugin detail, and the authoritative state read render here. The UI-29 trust/package gate remains open, so catalog, install, local-package import, and activation controls stay unavailable; no catalog exists (a catalog is supplied only by the Core — none is published); no invocation or execution surface exists (the D-13/D-14 gate and the Core Master Blueprint §10.2 runtime proof).
list.emptyAllBody: No user-installed plugin exists yet. The list renders only what the Core reports — no example plugin, no catalog, and no install control is fabricated.
list.trustNote: Trust renders only what the Core returns: a trust state the Core does not return renders Unknown — never Verified. A digest match is not publisher trust; a signature is not proof of safe behavior; a downloaded source is not verified; a WASM sandbox label is not trust.
list.failureTitle: The plugin list could not be read
list.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the list read. Nothing was changed; the list stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
list.unknownTitle: The plugin list read did not return a usable answer
list.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the list is empty or that the read failed — refresh to read again.
list.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.

detail.gateNote: The UI-29 trust/package gate remains open: catalog, install, activation, and removal controls stay unavailable, and the permission-review flow that gates activation stays withheld with them. This surface renders Core-owned reads only: nothing here installs, enables, updates, removes, or revokes anything.
detail.executionGateNote: No invocation or execution surface exists: plugin execution is withheld by the D-13/D-14 gate, and the Core Master Blueprint §10.2 runtime proof stands unresolved. No invocation control, invocation state, or invocation-derived record is rendered here — nothing is invented for it.
detail.stateNote: This is the family's authoritative state endpoint (a pure query). Events are never the source of truth; this read is. A lost response on any lifecycle action reconciles here by the plugin/package identity — never by a timeout, never a local guess.
detail.toggleDisabledReason: The UI-29 trust/package gate withholds activation controls: enabling a plugin is activation, and it stays unavailable until the gate's own recorded act. Nothing here flips a lifecycle state.
detail.toggleShapeNote: The Core serves one state-toggle member covering both directions via its target state. A lost response reconciles through the authoritative state read before any retry — never a local flip, never an optimistic state change.
detail.updateDisabledReason: No served surface supplies a target package version reference: a catalog exists only when the Core supplies one (none is published), and the update's fresh permission review — which any permission change triggers before an update may complete — has no producer on this Core. Nothing here fabricates an update target.
detail.removeDisabledReason: The UI-29 trust/package gate withholds removal controls. Removal would be a high-risk action confirmed explicitly (scope and effects stated) and Core-confirmed; no such flow is wired here.
detail.removeRevokeOpenNote: Whether removing a plugin and revoking its grants are the same or distinct effects is recorded OPEN — the Core's contract decides. This surface asserts neither, and no copy here promises either answer.
detail.revokeDisabledReason: Grant revocation is the user's explicit high-risk act through the Core's defined path; this milestone's transport carries the family's read members only, so no revocation caller is wired here. A retry never re-grants, and a denial stands until your own explicit act.
detail.overviewDistinctNote: The lifecycle states are distinct and stay distinct: Disabled (your action) is not Grants revoked, Grants revoked is not Trust revoked, and Trust revoked is not either — each renders its own state, never merged, never shown as a milder one. A failure state is never shown as a user-action state, and a user action is never shown as a failure.
detail.overviewTrustNote: Verified, Trusted, and Installed appear only after the corresponding Core evidence and policy conditions are met. This surface renders Core-returned values only — an absent verification state is never rendered as a verified one, and a trust state the Core does not return renders Unknown, never Verified.
detail.overviewFailureNote: The typed failure states (quota-terminated, crash, compatibility failure, trust revocation) render only as the Core returns them, never computed here. On this Core no invocation path exists (the execution gate) and no admission verification machinery is wired, so no failure record is producible — the absence is the honest state, never a fabricated failure.
detail.manifestAbsentTitle: The Core serves no manifest for this record
detail.manifestAbsentBody: The manifest member is optional on the published plugin record, and no manifest-examination path exists on this Core, so the served record carries none. The manifest fields (manifest version, plugin identity and version, publisher reference, artifact digest and signature, ABI version, requested capabilities, compatibility range, declared resource needs, license/SBOM reference, lifecycle state) render here exactly as the Core returns them once a served manifest exists — no manifest is fabricated.
detail.manifestUntrustedNote: Manifest text is untrusted data: rendered, never executed. It cannot grant permissions, mint capabilities, or change system instructions, and no plugin-supplied content executes in any rendered surface here.
detail.manifestResourceNote: The surface displays only Core-returned, proven limits where any limit is shown: per-instruction CPU/fuel quota is not assumed, and a wall-clock timeout is not fuel — a declared resource need is a declaration, and the Core's enforcement is the only authority.
detail.capabilitiesAbsentTitle: No granted-capability record is served here
detail.capabilitiesAbsentBody: The served record carries no granted-capability member, and no capability catalogue is published (the capability class rides the family only). The granted set of record starts empty at install and changes only through the Core's own acts — nothing is invented here.
detail.capabilitiesNeverGrantNote: A plugin can never grant itself permissions: the user grants and denies, and the Core mediates and enforces. Every grant is explicit, scoped, revocable, and auditable; a declared capability name is data, never a grant.
detail.capabilitiesReviewNote: The permission-review flow that gates enabling — one explicit grant or deny per requested capability, the data-egress description shown before anything is granted, Escape cancels without implying either — is activation-adjacent and stays withheld while the UI-29 trust/package gate is open.
detail.compatibilityAbsentTitle: No compatibility record is served here
detail.compatibilityAbsentBody: The Core serves no ABI or compatibility result for this record: the manifest member is absent (so no declared ABI version or compatibility range is served) and the Core returns no compatibility determination. The mismatch and update availability render here where the Core reports them — never computed.
detail.compatibilityAbiNote: The plugin's ABI version is separate from the host capability version; the Core's compatibility check is authoritative, an unknown required capability is rejected Core-side, and this surface performs no compatibility determination of its own.
detail.digestNoPackageTitle: No package record is served here
detail.digestNoPackageBody: The served record carries no package member, so no package verification state renders. The package verification states render exactly as the Core returns them once a served package exists — never computed, never inferred.
detail.digestVerificationNote: Every verification state here is Core-returned and rendered as returned: an absent member renders Unavailable and is never presented as verified. On this Core the served package carries the package reference alone — no verification machinery is wired — so the verification members render their honest absence.
detail.digestTrustWordNote: A digest establishes content identity relative to compared bytes only — never publisher authorization, authenticity, safety, or factual truth. A signature is not proof of safe behavior. A WASM sandbox label is defense in depth, not the trust boundary: the Core's authorization is. Trust revoked is distinct from Disabled and from Grants revoked, wherever the Core reports it.
detail.logsAbsentTitle: No sanitized diagnostics are served here
detail.logsAbsentBody: No published member serves plugin diagnostics for this family yet, so no log content renders. Missing and unavailable diagnostics are labeled honestly — nothing is reconstructed or substituted.
detail.logsRedactionNote: Redaction is the Core's duty; this surface never displays unredacted raw output. What may never appear here: secret values of any kind (a named secret-handle's name only, never its value), raw logs, runtime internals, stack traces, or memory contents, raw plugin output or raw provider payloads as diagnostics, and any diagnostic the Core did not return.
detail.auditAbsentTitle: No plugin event record is served here
detail.auditAbsentBody: The plugin family's lifecycle events ride the Core's audit layer, and no published member serves them on this surface. The Activity & Audit destination renders the audit categories it is served — this tab renders nothing invented.
detail.auditSourceNote: Events are never the source of truth: the authoritative state endpoint above is. The Core's audit receipts ride the Core's audit layer — this surface mints no parallel journal.
detail.failureTitle: The plugin record could not be read
detail.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the plugin read. Nothing was changed; the page stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
detail.unknownTitle: The plugin read did not return a usable answer
detail.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof of any outcome — refresh to read again.
detail.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.
detail.notFoundTitle: No plugin answers to this address
detail.notFoundBody: The Core's typed refusal answers unknown and out-of-scope identities with the same response — existence is never inferred from a refusal. Go back to the plugin list and open a plugin from there.
